description: Advanced open source relational database, focused on standards compliance and extensibility.

pg-connect.title: Connect to the database
pg-connect.description: Opens the interactive psql client connected to a specific database, user and host.
examples: Connects to the meuapp database as postgres.
Connects using a connection URL.
warnings: Avoid putting the password in the URL in shared environments; use the PGPASSWORD variable or ~/.pgpass.

pg-list-databases.title: List databases
pg-list-databases.description: psql meta-command that lists all databases on the server.
examples: Lists databases with owner and encoding.

pg-connect-db.title: Switch database in psql
pg-connect-db.description: Connects to another database within the current psql session.
examples: Switches to the meuapp database.

pg-list-tables.title: List tables
pg-list-tables.description: Lists the tables in the current schema. Use \d <table> to see a table's columns.
examples: Lists the tables.
Shows columns, types and indexes of the usuarios table.

pg-create-database.title: Create database
pg-create-database.description: Creates a new database. You can set the owner and encoding.
examples: Creates the database with the owner and encoding set.

pg-drop-database.title: Drop database
pg-drop-database.description: Permanently deletes a database and all of its contents.
examples: Drops the database if it exists.
warnings: Irreversibly deletes ALL of the database's data.
Cannot run while there are active connections to the database.

pg-create-table.title: Create table
pg-create-table.description: Creates a table with columns, types and constraints (primary key, not null, etc.).
examples: Creates the usuarios table with an auto-increment id and a unique email.

pg-alter-table.title: Alter table
pg-alter-table.description: Modifies a table's structure: adds/drops columns, changes types or constraints.
examples: Adds the ativo column.
warnings: On large tables, some changes lock the table; plan maintenance windows.

pg-select.title: Query data
pg-select.description: Retrieves rows from one or more tables, with filtering, ordering and limit.
examples: The last 10 active users.

pg-insert.title: Insert data
pg-insert.description: Adds new rows to a table. RETURNING gives back generated values such as the id.
examples: Inserts and returns the generated id.

pg-update.title: Update data
pg-update.description: Changes values in existing rows. WHERE is essential to avoid updating the whole table.
examples: Deactivates only user 42.
warnings: UPDATE without WHERE changes ALL rows in the table.

pg-delete.title: Delete data
pg-delete.description: Removes rows from a table. Without WHERE, it deletes all rows.
examples: Removes expired sessions.
warnings: DELETE without WHERE deletes ALL rows.
Consider a transaction (BEGIN) so you can undo it with ROLLBACK.

pg-join.title: Join tables (JOIN)
pg-join.description: Combines rows from two tables based on a relationship condition.
examples: Counts orders per user, including those with no orders (LEFT JOIN).

pg-create-index.title: Create index
pg-create-index.description: Creates an index to speed up lookups on columns used in WHERE and JOIN.
examples: Speeds up lookups by email.
Creates the index without blocking writes to the table.
warnings: Indexes speed up reads, but slow down writes and take up space.

pg-explain.title: Analyze query plan
pg-explain.description: Shows a query's actual execution plan with timings, revealing bottlenecks and index usage.
examples: Reveals whether the query uses an index or does a sequential scan.
warnings: With ANALYZE, the query is ACTUALLY executed; be careful with INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.

pg-create-user.title: Create user/role
pg-create-user.description: Creates a login role (user). Then grant privileges with GRANT.
examples: Creates the app_user user.
warnings: Use strong passwords and grant only the necessary privileges (principle of least privilege).

pg-grant.title: Grant privileges
pg-grant.description: Grants permissions (SELECT, INSERT, ALL, etc.) on tables or databases to a role.
examples: Grants read and write permissions to app_user.
warnings: Avoid granting ALL PRIVILEGES when specific permissions are enough.

pg-dump.title: Database backup
pg-dump.description: Exports a database's structure and data to a file, enabling backup and migration.
examples: Backup in SQL format.
Custom format (compressed), restorable with pg_restore.
warnings: The file may contain sensitive data; store it securely.

pg-restore.title: Restore backup
pg-restore.description: Restores a database from a custom-format dump created by pg_dump.
examples: Restores the dump into an existing database.
warnings: --clean drops existing objects in the target before restoring.

pg-vacuum.title: Maintenance (VACUUM)
pg-vacuum.description: Reclaims space from dead rows and updates statistics used by the query planner.
examples: Cleans up and updates statistics for the usuarios table.
warnings: VACUUM FULL locks the table; avoid it during peak hours.

pg-active-queries.title: View active connections
pg-active-queries.description: Shows current connections, running queries and their state, useful for diagnostics.
examples: Lists queries currently running.

pg-createdb-cli.title: Create database from the command line
pg-createdb-cli.description: Command-line utility to create a database without opening psql.
examples: Creates the meuapp database.
